The separation via flash tanks and the cooling of the ammonia product requires a refrigeration utility. Retentate gas from the H membrane and remaining components following ammonia 2 purification are mixed to form fuel gas (Stream 20) that is mixed with ambient air (Stream 21) in the fired heater. Convective heat recovery on the hot flue gas stream generates steam (not depicted) and provides heat to other parts of the plant, resulting in a cooled flue gas (Stream 22) that is combined with the vent (Stream 23) from the triethylene glycol dryer used in the CO 2 compression and drying system as well as the ASU vent (Stream 26) and sent to the stack (Stream 24). The plant produces steam (Stream 27) at 399 °C (750 °F) and 10.7 MPa (1,550 psia). After being sent through the HP steam turbine, a portion is sent to the primary reformer and the remaining (Stream 28) is sent through a MP steam turbine.
